newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Health premium rise not automatic - Canberra.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Health premium rise not automatic - Canberra.

text.p: Australian Health Minister Michael Wooldridge said on Wednesday the mooted rises in Medibank Private's health insurance premiums would not be automatic.
"No rise is automatic," Wooldridge told reporters.

Newspapers on Wednesday reported that Australia's largest health fund, Medibank Private, had applied for increases in premiums averaging 15 percent, which would totally offset the government's planned tax rebate for people with top health cover.
Wooldridge said talk of wiping out the rebate was silly and that health premiums had been rising for 10 years under the previous Labor government.
When asked if present legislation made it hard for him to refuse rises before the results of the government's private health inquiry on February 28, he said: "It sure does."
But he said he had not received a formal application from Medibank Private to raise its insurance premiums.
"Nothing formal has come over my desk," Wooldridge told reporters.
Wooldridge said he had not received advice from either the department or the private health insurance advisory committee on the premium rise.

In the 1996/97 (July-June) budget the Liberal-National government announced tax incentives worth A$500 million a year to encourage people to take out private health insurance and to wean rich people off the public Medicare health system.
The government attributed recent health fund premium increases to falling fund membership and rises in medical and hospitalisation charges.
